cards.explanation: The answer is Greeks. Verse 19 says the scattered believers were speaking the message only to Jews. Then these men from Cyprus and Cyrene get to Antioch and start speaking to the Greeks as well. That's a real change in who hears it, friends. I think those Greeks were glad to hear it.

The answer is the good news about the Lord Jesus. Acts 11:20 says it plainly: they were proclaiming the good news about the Lord Jesus. These men travel to a new city, and Jesus is the whole message. When the message is that good, friends, you don't need a second topic.

The answer is False. Acts 11:21 says a great number of people believed and turned to the Lord. That's the opposite of a handful, bakers. The men from Cyprus and Cyrene walk into Antioch, and the hand of the Lord is with them. I'd call that a very full church directory.

The answer is False. Acts 11:23 says Barnabas saw the grace of God and rejoiced. Barnabas, the man the Jerusalem church sent, walks into Antioch and is simply glad. I think he had a very hard time keeping that smile off his face.

The answer is to remain in the Lord with all their hearts. The BSB says Barnabas encouraged them all to "…abide in the Lord with all their hearts." That's the same idea as remain, friends. He doesn't ask for half a heart or a heart on weekends. All their hearts, in one big batch.

The answer is True. Verse 24 says a great number of people were brought to the Lord. That follows the first great number in verse 21. Barnabas, described as a good man full of the Holy Spirit and faith, is there, and the number keeps growing. Church growth doesn't get much clearer than that, bakers.

The answer is back to Antioch. Acts 11:26 says Barnabas found Saul and brought him back to Antioch. Saul is the man Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for. Antioch is where the church was growing, friends, and now two teachers are there together.

The answer is Christians. Acts 11:26 says the disciples were first called Christians at Antioch. That's the first time the name shows up in this story. Antioch gets to say it was there when the name started, friends.

The answer is a great famine. Acts 11:28 says Agabus predicted through the Spirit that a great famine would sweep across the whole world. Agabus is one of the prophets who came down from Jerusalem. The same verse says it happened under Claudius. His prediction gets confirmed, bakers, and the disciples act on it.
The answer is Judea. Verse 29 says the disciples decided to send relief to the brothers living in Judea. Each one gave according to his ability. That's a kind way to spend a decision, friends.

The answer is False. Acts 11:29 says the disciples decided to send relief, each according to his ability. So the gift fits the giver. I think that means nobody has to be embarrassed by a smaller gift, bakers. That's a good way to run a collection.

The answer is Barnabas and Saul. Acts 11:30 says the disciples sent their gifts to the elders with Barnabas and Saul. These are the two who taught in Antioch for a full year. Now they also carry the relief. It's a lot of jobs for two men, friends.
